scenariosList.title: Two-Thread Shared Counter Race
scenariosList.objective: Demonstrate a lost update when two threads concurrently increment a shared variable without synchronization.
scenariosList.description: Two worker threads execute a decomposed increment (READ -> ADD LOCAL -> WRITE) on a shared counter. With round-robin interleaving, both read the initial value 0 before either writes, causing one update to be completely lost.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Unsynchronized reads and writes across threads cause data races and lost updates. Decomposing high-level operations exposes their non-atomic nature.

scenariosList.title: Three-Thread Shared Counter Race
scenariosList.objective: Observe severe state corruption when three concurrent threads increment the same shared counter.
scenariosList.description: Three concurrent worker threads interleave reads and writes to 'counter'. Expected final result is 3, but interleavings produce 1 or 2.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: Expected: counter = 3. Actual: counter = 1 or 2 depending on interleaving.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Contention escalates rapidly with more threads. Without synchronization, multiple updates get overwritten.

scenariosList.title: Mutex-Protected Shared Counter
scenariosList.objective: Verify that acquiring a mutex lock guarantees atomic execution of critical sections and eliminates lost updates.
scenariosList.description: Two threads increment 'counter', but enclose the read, compute, and write instructions inside a mutex lock and unlock pair.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Mutual exclusion ensures only one thread executes inside the critical section at any given time, preventing data races.

scenariosList.title: High Lock Contention
scenariosList.objective: Observe thread blocking, FIFO queue formation, and wake-up transitions under high mutex contention.
scenariosList.description: Three threads contend for the same mutex 'printer_lock'. Watch the second and third threads become BLOCKED and enter the waiting queue.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: All threads complete in FIFO queue order without data corruption.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: When a lock is held, contending threads sleep in the wait queue, preserving CPU cycles and guaranteeing ordered resumption.

scenariosList.title: Counting Semaphore Resource Limiter
scenariosList.objective: Demonstrate how a counting semaphore regulates concurrent access to a resource pool with capacity = 2.
scenariosList.description: Four worker threads attempt to access a database connection pool with only 2 available connections. Two threads acquire immediately; the remaining two block until connections are released.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: At most 2 threads hold connections concurrently. Counter never exceeds limits.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Unlike binary mutexes, counting semaphores maintain a counter, permitting multiple concurrent holders up to capacity.

scenariosList.title: Producer-Consumer Bounded Buffer
scenariosList.objective: Implement the classic bounded-buffer problem using empty/full counting semaphores and a mutex.
scenariosList.description: A producer generates items into a 3-slot buffer. A consumer extracts items. Counting semaphores prevent buffer overflow and underflow.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: Buffer size strictly remains between 0 and 3. Producers block when full, consumers block when empty.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Coordination requires both mutual exclusion (buffer access) and condition signaling (space available vs item available).

scenariosList.title: Dining Philosophers Deadlock
scenariosList.objective: Demonstrate a five-way circular wait deadlock when all philosophers pick up their left fork simultaneously.
scenariosList.description: Five philosophers sit at a round table with 5 shared forks. Each philosopher first acquires their left fork, then their right fork. Under round-robin scheduling, all pick up their left fork simultaneously and freeze waiting for their right fork.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: Deadlock detected! Wait-for graph forms a 5-node directed cycle.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Circular wait is the 4th Coffman condition for deadlock. Symmetrical resource acquisition leads directly to livelock or deadlock.

scenariosList.title: Dining Philosophers Deadlock-Free
scenariosList.objective: Eliminate deadlock in Dining Philosophers using an asymmetric resource ordering strategy.
scenariosList.description: By making the last philosopher pick up their forks in reverse order (right before left, or lowest-index first), the circular wait condition is permanently broken.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: All philosophers successfully think, eat, and release forks without deadlock.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Breaking symmetry prevents circular wait, ensuring at least one philosopher can always acquire both forks and make progress.

scenariosList.title: Two-Mutex Circular Wait Deadlock
scenariosList.objective: Illustrate textbook circular wait deadlock between two threads acquiring two locks in opposite order.
scenariosList.description: Thread 1 acquires Mutex A, then requests Mutex B. Thread 2 acquires Mutex B, then requests Mutex A. Both threads become permanently blocked.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: Deadlock detected! Wait-for graph displays a 2-node cycle: Thread 1 <-> Thread 2.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: When locks are acquired in arbitrary or reverse order, circular dependencies can freeze the system.

scenariosList.title: Deadlock-Free Lock Hierarchy
scenariosList.objective: Demonstrate how enforcing a strict lock acquisition hierarchy prevents circular wait deadlocks.
scenariosList.description: Both Thread 1 and Thread 2 acquire Mutex A first, then Mutex B. Because both respect the global hierarchy, circular waiting is mathematically impossible.
scenariosList.expectedOutcome: Both threads complete their critical sections successfully without deadlock.
scenariosList.keyTakeaway: Enforcing a global total order on lock acquisitions eliminates circular wait (one of Coffman's four deadlock conditions).
